changes.after: Check that typed text is a whole number the program can use.

before: Console.ReadLine reads one line from standard input and can return null when no more input is available. It does not automatically convert digits into numbers.
int.TryParse(raw, out int count) returns true when raw can be read as an int and false otherwise. The out declaration creates a variable for the parsed result.
On failure, this overload sets count to zero. Do not mistake that zero for a successful input. Branch on the returned Boolean first.
A valid integer can still be unsuitable for your task. After parsing succeeds, a condition such as count >= 0 can enforce your application rule.
Expected behavior from this example: input 12 produces Accepted: 12; input cat produces the error message. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer task: Try 0, -2, cat, and an out-of-range whole number. Separate parsing failure from a valid number rejected by your rule. You may trace it on paper if no C# toolchain is installed; reading completion does not certify a run.
after: Console.ReadLine() reads one line of typed text. It can return null when no input remains. Digits arrive as text, not as a number.
Parsing means reading a value from text. int.TryParse tries to read an int. It returns true when it succeeds. The out part puts the result in count.
If this TryParse call fails, it returns false and sets count to zero. Check the true or false result; zero alone does not tell you whether parsing worked.
This program accepts zero or a positive number. The && means both checks must pass. It checks count >= 0 only after TryParse succeeds.
For input 12, parsing succeeds and 12 is at least zero. The program prints Accepted: 12.
Input -2 is a valid int, but it is below zero. The program shows its error message because the second check fails.

before.question: The input is "-2". Why does the error message appear?
choices: TryParse cannot parse any minus sign.
The integer is parsed, but the separate nonnegative rule rejects it.
The parsed value is automatically converted to zero.
before.explanation: Parsing succeeds for -2; the second condition fails because -2 is below zero.

after.question: Why does input -2 show the error message?
choices: TryParse cannot read a minus sign.
It is a whole number, but the program only accepts zero or more.
TryParse always changes negative numbers to zero.
after.explanation: TryParse succeeds. The separate count >= 0 check fails.
